items.title: July’s 0.1% CPI rise is misleading. Energy prices fell because CPI compares monthly average prices. But oil and gasoline rose sharply during July after starting the month at depressed levels. That means July CPI still reflects May's oil price collapse, not July's sharp rebound.
items.content:
July’s 0.1% CPI rise is misleading. Energy prices fell because CPI compares monthly average prices. But oil and gasoline rose sharply during July after starting the month at depressed levels. That means July CPI still reflects May's oil price collapse, not July's sharp rebound.
— Peter Schiff (@PeterSchiff) Aug 12, 2026
